title: Are we there yet? A machine learning architecture to predict organotropic metastases
summary: A tree-based machine-learning architecture classified metastatic sites from primary-tumor RNA profiles and identified overlapping enriched processes across several metastatic destinations. The analysis uses retrospective TCGA data and is limited to eligible cancer types and annotated cases; it does not establish prospective prediction.
ai_technology: Statistical feature selection and tree-based classifiers for metastatic-site prediction from RNA profiles
organization: University of Georgia; Weill Cornell Medicine

evidence.tested: Across 35 cancer-site pairs, the study reported mean precision, recall, F1 and accuracy of 0.82 and overlapping enriched processes for four metastatic sites.
evidence.unknown: A 30% holdout from TCGA is retrospective internal validation; findings cover 16 of 33 studied cancer types and depend on annotated profiles.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classifiers use primary-tumor transcript features to predict metastatic sites; selected features support pathway-enrichment analysis.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results; publication date and catalog comparisons checked.
